title: Finite sets in a bounded-above free complex lie in a bounded finite-free subcomplex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $F^\bullet$ be an integer cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and assume $F^n=0$ for all $n>b$ for some integer $b$. Assume each $F^n$ is free, meaning isomorphic to a direct sum of copies of $A$. For any finite list of pairs $(n_j,x_j)$ with $n_j\in\mathbf Z$ and $x_j\in F^{n_j}$, there is a subcomplex $G^\bullet\subset F^\bullet$ containing every $x_j$ such that $G^n=0$ outside some finite interval and every $G^n$ is finite free, meaning isomorphic to $A^{r_n}$ for a finite integer $r_n\ge0$. A subcomplex here means a choice of submodules $G^n\subset F^n$ with $d_F^n(G^n)\subset G^{n+1}$, equipped with the restricted differentials.

proof.text: Choose a lower degree a at most b+1 and at most every input degree, by induction on the input list and taking minima. Strengthen the assertion to P(t): every finite set of homogeneous elements in degrees at least t is contained in a finite-free subcomplex supported in [t,b]. Prove P(t) for t at most b+1 by descending integer induction. At t=b+1 all input elements are zero by the upper vanishing bound, so choose the zero submodules, each isomorphic to A^0.

source.place: Tag 0FNR, lemma-complex-bounded-above-free-colim-bounded-finite-free; proof, opening descending induction and zero-complex base case; make the lower support bound explicit

proof.text: Fix $t\le b$ and assume $P(t+1)$. By freeness choose coordinates $\phi:F^t\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{i\in I}A$, whose elements are finitely supported coefficient functions. Let $J\subset I$ be the union of the supports of $\phi(x_j)$ over those inputs with $n_j=t$. This is finite, including when there are no such inputs. Write $e_i=\phi^{-1}(\delta_i)$ and let $E\subset F^t$ be the image under $\phi^{-1}$ of the functions supported in $J$. Extension by zero gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $A^J\to E$, with inverse the restriction of $\phi$ to $J$: restriction followed by extension recovers a function supported in $J$, and extension followed by restriction recovers every tuple. Thus $E$ is finite free and contains every input of degree $t$.

source.place: Tag 0FNR, lemma-complex-bounded-above-free-colim-bounded-finite-free; proof, choose the basis b_j and the finite subset J prime

proof.text: Let y be the finite set of basis vectors indexed by J from step 2, so E is the span of y. Form the finite set of homogeneous pairs (t+1,d_F^t(z)) for z in y. Taking these differential images themselves as the inputs to the induction hypothesis replaces the redundant second coordinate expansion in the source proof.

source.place: Tag 0FNR, lemma-complex-bounded-above-free-colim-bounded-finite-free; proof, choose the basis c_k and the finite subset K prime controlling the differentials

proof.text: Apply P(t+1) to the union of the differential-image pairs from step 3 and the original pairs whose degree is strictly greater than t. This is a finite set and all its degrees are at least t+1. Obtain H supported in [t+1,b] with finite-free terms. Define G^t=E and G^n=H^n for n different from t. In particular G is zero below t because H is zero below t+1. This is an application of the descending induction hypothesis only.

source.place: Tag 0FNR, lemma-complex-bounded-above-free-colim-bounded-finite-free; proof, application of the induction hypothesis to the c_k and the remaining original inputs; definition of G

proof.text: For n<t the domain G^n is zero. At n=t, every generator z in y has d_F^t(z) in H^{t+1} by the choice of the induction inputs. Since E is the span of y, the span universal property (equivalently the inverse image of H^{t+1} under the differential) gives d_F^t(E) contained in H^{t+1}. For n>t use the differential stability of H. The cochain identity of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is inherited by restricted differentials, as equality of submodule elements is equality in the ambient module.

source.place: Tag 0FNR, lemma-complex-bounded-above-free-colim-bounded-finite-free; proof, verification that the displayed G is a subcomplex, including the splice differential

proof.text: The constructed $G$ contains the original inputs of degree $t$ by step 2 and those of higher degree by step 4. Its degree-$t$ term is $A^J$, its higher terms are the finite-free terms of $H$, and its lower terms are zero, isomorphic to $A^0$. All its terms vanish outside $[t,b]$, so $P(t)$ holds. After the finitely many induction steps down to $a$, $P(a)$ supplies the required subcomplex for the original list; enumerate each finite coordinate set to identify its coordinate module with $A^{r_n}$ for its cardinality $r_n$.
